A protocol is a NAMED PROTOCOL PLUS ITS PARAMETERS -- never a raw time series.
Transient experiments make the design space a function space, since one of the
knobs is when transients fire, but real transient experiments are
parameterised, so the parameterisation is the representation.
THE SAME OBJECT is stored alongside executed data and emitted by experiment
design. One representation, so closing the loop later is plumbing rather than
Available: prbs | pulse_train | temperature_ramp | step_change | multi_pulse |
steady_state. Each owns its own parameter space; the schema enforces per
protocol. Two worked examples below -- keep the one you need.
$comment_prbs: waveform is REQUIRED and comes in three forms. What all three deliver is the
ability to reconstruct the actual perturbation; what differs is how much of it
survived.
lfsr          register_length, taps, seed, bit_period_s, n_bits.
Three integers regenerate the sequence exactly. Shown above.
n_bits = 2**register_length - 1 is one full period; truncating
loses the balanced-spectrum property that makes PRBS worth
using in the first place.
recorded      switch_times_s: the schedule as executed, plus an optional
initial_level. Use this when the valve controller can log what
it did. A randomised-dwell train has no generator state, so the
executed schedule IS the reproducible object.
reconstructed tracer_channel and reason. The honest fallback when neither of
the above exists and the inlet has to be recovered from an
inert tracer. Everything downstream inherits that
reconstruction's assumptions, so the reason is not optional.
If you are reaching for the third form, that is an instrument work item rather
than a metadata one -- logging the schedule is usually a small change.
There is also an optional `label` for the operator's own sequence name. It is
recorded verbatim and trusted for nothing: in the first real dataset the
project ingested, the identical label appeared on five runs at five different
temperatures.
$comment_base: The steady operating point the perturbation is applied around. Separate from
parameters because it is shared across every protocol, while parameters differ.
$comment_time_base: UTC with an explicit offset. This is what lets simultaneously-acquired MS, IR,
and XAS streams be ALIGNED rather than merely parallel -- which is the
difference between a multimodal dataset and three datasets.
